---
title: "Troubleshooting"
subtitle: "When the call, the tool, the account, or the output is not behaving"
---

Almost every problem during the course is one of four things: the call, a missing part of the prompt, a tool limit, or an account that is not ready. Find yours below.

## The call is the problem

- **I cannot see the shared screen, or it is too small to read.** Say so in the chat. Make the presentation fill your call tab, and ask the instructor for larger text if it still does not read.
- **I cannot open the slides link, or Copy prompt does nothing.** Say so in the chat. The instructor pastes each prompt in the chat too, and you can copy it from there. On a phone, select the text and copy it by hand.
- **I missed what was pasted in the chat.** Ask in the chat and the instructor pastes it again. Someone who joins late may not see earlier messages.
- **The chat moves too fast.** Type your answer and send it; the instructor reads a few out. You do not need to follow every message.
- **My breakout room did not open, or my partner did not join.** Tell the instructor in the chat. The step has a version that needs no partner: you do it on your own and type the result in the chat.
- **I cannot talk or type in the chat right now.** Say so by any means you have. Nothing here is graded, and every answer you were asked for can be given later in the chat.
- **I joined late.** Ask in the chat for what was pasted so far, and carry on from the slide the instructor is on.
- **My screen is too small for the call and my assistant.** Keep the call on one device and your assistant on another.

## The output is the problem

| What you see | Why it happens | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Generic, could be about anyone | The tool only knows what is in the conversation | Add the case facts and the purpose. See the **Context** part of the framework |
| Long, hedged, padded | Nothing told it the length or the register | Add a word limit and "No hedging phrases" under **Constraints** |
| A different structure every time | No template | Give the exact headings under **Format** |
| A number, dose, or date changed | The tool rewrote a value it should have copied | Say "copy all numbers exactly as given", then check every number against the source. You supply numbers; the tool never chooses them |
| Something appears that you never gave it | The tool filled a gap with something plausible | Use "Use ONLY the facts below. If something needed is missing, write [MISSING: what]" |
| A citation you cannot find | Citations can be fabricated | Treat it as fabricated until you open the source yourself |
| It answers a nearby question, not yours | Your question was leading or too broad | Ask neutrally, one question, with the constraint stated |
| Different answers to the same question | Normal: the same question does not always give the same words | Fix the format so results are comparable, and treat disagreement as a reason to verify |
| The chat has gotten worse as it got longer | Early instructions drop out of view | Start a new chat. Paste your fact sheet and constraints again |
| It refuses or adds warnings to a medical task | The wording read as a request for a decision | Ask for a draft, a summary, or a rewording of facts you supply, and keep the decision with you |

## The account or the tool is the problem

- **I cannot open a literature-grounded tool (Vera Health or another).** Nothing depends on it. Use your assistant's search or citation mode, or a plain literature search such as PubMed, as [Module 3](../day1/m3-choosing-tools.qmd#second-option) describes. Do not use anyone else's login.
- **I hit the free limit.** Batch related questions into one detailed prompt, wait, or switch to another tool. See the quota section in [Module 3](../day1/m3-choosing-tools.qmd).
- **The tool is blocked on my hospital network.** Use your own device on your own connection, **with synthetic cases only**. Never work around an institutional block with real patient information.
- **Arabic output looks off.** Ask for Modern Standard Arabic in simple wording. Medical terms and register vary, so a fluent reader must check every line before a patient sees it.
- **Formatting breaks when I paste.** Ask for plain text, with tables written as lists.

## The problem is what I pasted

- **I pasted something that could identify a patient.** Stop, write down what and where, and report it through your institution's process. See "If it already happened" on the [privacy checklist](privacy-checklist.qmd).
- **A colleague did.** The same steps apply, and the [privacy module](../day3/m7-privacy.qmd) has the conversation to have.
